ordinary_current_main.design: Six fixed baseline repetitions of the actual failing two-core test. All outcomes retained. This is a correctness diagnosis of an observed CI failure, not a performance comparison or a retry until green.

private_baseline_control.design: One negative timing control: change only private board timer period from1ms to1s. Worker computation, concurrency/migration/output/frame assertions and all test budgets remain unchanged. This controlled board differs from the ordinary current-main run, whose six repetitions passed. No claim of natural local reproduction.

fixed_controls.design: Six fixed repetitions of both unchanged kernel scheduler assertions, then Go vet. One private one-second timer control checks migration separately and retains every original concurrency/output/frame assertion. A nonzero private-control exit remains a negative result, never a normal test pass. No compiler, stdlib, proof rule, timer or timeout change in product sources.

runs.label: private-slow-timer
runs.note: The one-second private timer removes the normal concurrency trigger. All original assertion failures remain visible. Only normal unchanged-source test runs supply the product pass gate.

conclusion: Ordinary current main passed all six local repetitions. The CI log remains an actual failure. The private one-second timer exposes dependence on interrupt pacing: old migration/concurrency assertions fail, while the corrected dispatch policy passes every unchanged assertion under that same private timer. This does not prove a unique CI timing cause or any compiler miscompile.
product_scope: Only the Go test fixture dispatch eligibility changes. Compiler, stdlib, timer period, worker computation, test assertions and budgets remain unchanged.
